# Resolve-ZbxTrapperEndpoint

## SYNOPSIS

Finds the trapper a host's values must be sent to.

## SYNTAX

```
Resolve-ZbxTrapperEndpoint [-InputObject] <ZabbixHost> [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Resolve-ZbxTrapperEndpoint cmdlet says where values for each host piped in must go: for a host monitored by a proxy, the proxy's own address and port; otherwise the server's trapper, the one given to Connect-ZbxServer -Trapper or else the active high-availability node's. It is the rule the Zabbix frontend uses, and never guesses a port. It writes one object per host with HostName, HostId, Server, Address and Port, and sends nothing to the trapper itself.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Find where to send a host's values

```powershell
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01' | Resolve-ZbxTrapperEndpoint
```

The server monitors web-01 itself, so the answer is the server's trapper.

### Example 2: Find the trappers of a group's hosts

```powershell
Get-ZbxHost -Group 'Linux servers' | Resolve-ZbxTrapperEndpoint | Select-Object HostName, Address, Port
```

The proxy proxy-01 monitors db-01, so its values go to the proxy's address.
